recEDO3WWWhzVkwgI.Bio: Matt Presti is a metascientist, musician, and host of The Exploration of Consciousness (TEC) podcast, known for his long-running study of the science and philosophy of Walter Russell. His work centers on light, universal law, and cosmology, and on InnerVerse he has explored Russell's teachings alongside critiques of mainstream physics.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "A documentary aimed at dimensional delusion", "body": "Chance Garton welcomes back Matt Presti to unpack his film Dispelling Dimensional Madness, a ten year project built from more than two hundred hours of research. Presti argues that belief in higher dimensions is not ancient wisdom but a recent invention traced through spiritualism, scientific romance and academic mathematics. He says the hardest part of making the film was that he could find no other detractors, only papers written by people friendly to the idea. His stated purpose is blunt, to hold people's feet back to the ground and get their heads back into the life they are actually living."}, {"title": "Where the fourth dimension actually came from", "body": "The conversation walks the history in detail. Henry More coined the term fourth dimension in his 1671 Enchiridion Metaphysicum, opposing Cartesian dualism and describing a spiritual substance he called essential spissitude, essentially Plato's realm of ideal forms. Jean le Rond d'Alembert was the first mathematician to fold time in as a fourth dimension. Presti also cites Gerard Hickson's book King's Dethroned, which argues time cannot be a fourth dimension because length, breadth and width are not independent of one another, while Einstein treats his dimensions as if they were."}, {"title": "Seances, fraud and the birth of the fifth dimension", "body": "Presti traces the popular version of higher dimensions to the spiritualist craze of 1850s to 1880s London, which he calls New Age 1.0. Johann Zollner of Leipzig University hired the medium Henry Slade, recommended by Helena Blavatsky, who wrote on a chalk slate with his foot and claimed spirits in the fourth dimension were doing it. Slade was caught, fled Europe and died broke. Sir William Crookes, inventor of the cathode ray tube, was fooled at seances by a woman dressed as a ghost called Katie King while grieving his brother."}, {"title": "Escapism, ascension symptoms and honesty", "body": "Both men separate healthy escape, a walk in the woods or a sitcom, from what Presti calls toxic escapism, the Gnostic sense that this place is a hell hole to flee. Chance pushes back gently on the flat earth example, noting most flat earthers he knows are homesteading rather than waiting for the ice wall. They then criticize ascension cults that rebrand poor health and unprocessed trauma as five dimensional ascension symptoms. Presti invokes Carl Jung, saying wholeness comes from integrating your own noetic darkness, and Chance argues honesty is the actual key to health."}, {"title": "Mind as the fulcrum and hermeticism as the alternative", "body": "The positive case is Walter Russell's cosmology, where light is the one substance and mind is the non dimensional cause. Presti reads from Atomic Suicide by Walter and Lao Russell on everything being three, then extends the point through fulcrums, the door jamb, the guitar bridge, the seesaw, motion always moving on stillness at ninety degrees. Chance connects this to his biofield tuning work and to mind as the mental plane rather than a physical ether. Presti closes by naming himself a hermeticist and telling listeners their own mind is the fulcrum and the savior."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Matt Presti returns to InnerVerse to discuss his new documentary, Dispelling Dimensional Madness: A Refutation of Gnosticism, Mythematics, and New Age Scientism. As one of the key thinkers responsible for restoring the legacy of illuminated physicist Walter Russell, Matt Presti is a powerful force for logic and knowledge, and in this episode we will put Simulation Theory and other such nonsense to the Sword (of truth).
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In the oversized Plus+ Extension, we cover Alice in Wonderland's criticism of imaginary math, ghosts and spirits, hypercubes and tesseracts, Ma'at and myth, the nature of time, and seeing God by playing with magnets.
